“The Armed Forces maintain full control over all their battlefield gains. What the enemy promotes as victories is nothing but imaginary heroics intended to please its masters, just like its malicious tactics, which our people are well aware of, whether along the western coast or in other areas,” Houthi-aligned Yemeni Armed Forces spokesman Yahya Saree has said.
Saree’s comments follow the Saudi-aligned Aden government’s claims Monday that its forces had successfully executed a counteroffensive in areas recently won by the Houthis, including Bab al-Mandab and Mocha, as part of Operation “[Dawn of Yemen](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75676).”
Saree reported that over 200 enemy troops had been killed or wounded in strikes on enemy positions in the areas of Ras al-Arah and al-Saqiya in southwestern Yemen, and that the Armed Forces were carrying out attacks in al-Jawf and Marib provinces, killing scores of mercenaries and destroying [multiple vehicles](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75690).
💬Mercenary forces’ attempts to infiltrate Bab al-Mandab were met with a “decisive response” and “strong defense” and were supressed, and enemies were forced to retreat without achieving any battlefield success, highlighting Saudi Arabia’s inability to change the military equation in strategic areas on the battlefield, the spokesman said.

events.text:
🤥 Trump's challenge: More crude, same high diesel prices – Hormuz flows and US output may not help
Diesel prices are set to remain elevated in the US and globally through 2027, Goldman Sachs warns.
Even as some crude continues to flow through the Strait of Hormuz and US oil production hits a record 13.95 million barrels per day, that doesn’t mean those volumes will immediately translate into much-needed diesel.
🔴A 42-gallon barrel of US-refined crude yields about 19-20 gallons of gasoline and 11-13 gallons of ultra-low-sulfur distillate, most of which becomes diesel, Forbes explains
🔴US refineries already operate at around 96% of capacity, which has been declining in recent years. They can’t ramp up production overnight
🔴To make matters worse, US distillate inventories have fallen below 100 million barrels and may remain below the 2021–2025 five-year low through 2026 and most of 2027, EIA says
The global outlook is also grim, with major supplies disrupted in the Middle East, Russia, and China:
🔴Russia has restricted fuel exports following Ukrainian attacks on its refineries — part of Kiev’s strategy backed by its Western allies
🔴Middle Eastern refinery output and shipping have been disrupted by the war with Iran, launched by the US and Israel in February
🔴China has temporarily banned fuel exports to bolster domestic stocks amid geopolitical uncertainty
Europe is in an especially difficult position, having cut refining capacity over the past 15 years amid the green transition to just 14.4 million barrels per day. Donald Trump has twisted its arm into releasing some of its diesel reserves – but it's a drop in the bucket, experts say.
Diesel is expected to average above $40 a barrel in 2027 – more than twice their historical norm of around $20.

🛩🚀🇺🇸 US drone maker Anduril dives into submarine tech
 
The Trump administration-linked defense startup, which just lost one of its brand new Dive-LD unmanned drone submersibles to Iran, plans to pump $3.7B into a new shipbuilding facility in Sparrows Point, Maryland to assist in the production of America’s [nuclear-powered submarines](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74351).
Anduril promises the facility, set to be up and running by 2030 and to employ ~3.1k people, will “really reimagine how a shipyard is built and how this work is done.” That may be a veiled dig at traditional shipbuilding majors, who are short up to 250k skilled workers to complete subs the Pentagon has already [ordered](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72896).
The company’s new project comes in the wake of DoD chief Hegseth’s announcement that Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey, Elon Musk and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich had been tapped to spearhead a new project to secure “absolute technological dominance” in future [US wars](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75490).

events.text:
🤥📊 Trump’s Golden Dome risks turning into tin strainer amid funding woes
 
The Trump administration’s modern-day reboot of Reagan’s Strategic Defense Initiative could cost between $1.2T and $3.6T to build and operate, per independent analyses by the Congressional Budget Office and the American Enterprise Institute.
But even the Pentagon’s own ‘modest’ projections of $185B may be out of America’s [price range. ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/68909)
DC Beltway media report that the DoD’s decision to pack Golden Dome funding into a $350B spending package that’s separate from Trump’s $1.5T proposed defense budget could leave the missile defense project without funds.
As of the start of the federal fiscal year (October 1), “the program has no money,” CSIS Missile Defense Project director Thomas Karako told The Hill.
💬“This stands or falls with FY-27 appropriations…that’s the single most urgent thing for Golden Dome. It is life and death from that standpoint. Without money there’s no program, it’s just PowerPoint slides,” he explained.
Congress already pumped $24.5B into the project in last year’s ‘Big Beautiful Bill’. The Pentagon now wants $17B more in the $350B package. But that money is under threat because of Congress’s Continuing Resolution stopgap funding measure – which funds the government by extending the previous year’s spending, thus effectively freezing out Golden Dome.
If Congress can’t find a way to get the money, “there is no Golden Dome because there is no funding,” Space Force Golden Dome program director Michael Guetlein said.

If the plane had continued on, the command center would have contacted Netanyahu, who would have to make the final decision on the fate of the plane and its 182 passengers and crew.
It wouldn’t have been for Israel to deploy a version of its Hannibal Directive – which instructs the IDF to do everything in its power, up to and including killing, to stop Israeli citizens from being kidnapped.[ The directive is known to have been used on October 7](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/61831).
✈️ [As for Flydubai Flight 1073](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75532), journalists have lingering questions about just what that incident was – an attempted hijacking by a lone wolf extremist, or a false flag and choreographed PR stunt by Netanyahu to blame Iran, strengthen Israeli-Gulf relations and generate global sympathy for Israel.
